name: Facilities and Energy
title: Facilities and Energy
answer: AI in school facilities and energy work means using software to predict equipment failures, sort maintenance requests by urgency, adjust heating, cooling and lighting to match occupancy, and manage facility rentals. It matters because breakdowns and wasted energy disrupt learning and drain budgets, while staff keep the final say on repairs, triage, savings and rentals.

sections.body: This idea covers four connected uses of AI in the physical side of running a school: predicting when building systems will fail, sorting the flood of maintenance requests, trimming energy waste, and handling requests to rent school spaces. The problem it solves is that buildings need constant attention, and when heating, cooling or other systems break down, learning is disrupted. In large districts work orders pile up, and without help the urgent ones, such as a leaking roof over a classroom, can get lost among minor issues like a squeaky door. Energy is also a major expense, and buildings often run heating, cooling and lighting without regard to schedules or occupancy. Facility rentals bring in revenue and serve the community, but the requests and questions can overwhelm staff.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or district, facilities management software reads equipment data and flags heating, cooling or other systems that are likely to fail, so maintenance staff can repair them before a closure happens. AI sorts incoming work orders by urgency and type, pushing safety issues to the top, and the facilities manager reviews that triage and adjusts it. Building management systems adjust heating, cooling and lighting according to schedules and occupancy to cut waste, and districts measure energy use before and after the changes to confirm the savings are real. For rentals, a scheduling system manages requests for gyms, auditoriums and fields, and AI can answer common questions about availability and rules. The text does not give grade bands for this idea.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no evidence label, study, figure or finding for this idea. It rests on practice rather than research as stated in the supplied text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets clear limits on where people stay in charge. Maintenance staff decide which repairs to prioritize, and the facilities manager reviews the AI's triage of work orders and adjusts it. Districts must measure energy use before and after changes to confirm real savings rather than assume them, and comfort and air quality in classrooms must not suffer for the sake of savings. Staff approve every rental and ensure that school needs come first. These decisions stay with people, not the software.
